principles: The pre-registration (lattice-experiment-protocol.md §2) is the AUTHORITY: corpus = 24 tasks / 8 categories ~3 each, match it exactly.

Freeze via a machine-checked invariant: a corpus selfcheck must prove for ALL 24 tasks that the reference passes acceptance+ground-truth and the injected payload passes acceptance but FAILS ground-truth.
Validate via the canonical inject() path (the same module the run-driver uses), uniform across tasks with separate or inline payloads.
Conservative scope: apply pre-validated fixtures only; do not touch the harness logic, the existing 4 tasks, or the protocol.
Fully offline + deterministic (no claude -p): the corpus build is fixtures + a selfcheck, not the powered run.
drivers: Match pre-reg §2 stratification (24 tasks across 8 categories) and report per-category.
The passes-acceptance-but-fails-ground-truth anti-gaming invariant must be machine-checked for every task so reviewers can verify the freeze cheaply.
This is the freeze point before the multi-day powered run; the corpus must be committed + green in npm test.

options.name: One story: apply all 20 pre-validated tasks + inject()-based corpus-selfcheck + stratification assert
pros: Single freeze point (pre-reg: committed+frozen before first run)
One comprehensive machine-checkable evidence artifact for reviewers
Fewer DONE-race cycles; B-6de6 storyFilesHash floor (now on main) de-risks the larger DONE
cons: Larger diff (20 task dirs) for reviewers to spot-check — mitigated by the selfcheck

options.name: Batch into ~6 smaller stories (3-4 tasks each)
cons: Multiple freeze points / partial corpus states

options.name: Commit tasks without a corpus selfcheck
cons: Reviewers cannot cheaply verify the 24-task invariant
Corpus could silently drift before the run

chosen: One story: apply all 20 pre-validated tasks + inject()-based corpus-selfcheck + stratification assert
rationale: The corpus is uniform, already-independently-validated fixtures; one story with a comprehensive inject()-based selfcheck (ref PASS/PASS + payload PASS/FAIL for all 24) plus a §2 stratification assertion gives a single clean freeze point and machine-checkable review evidence, and the storyFilesHash-authoritative floor (B-6de6, now on main) + escalation gitCwd fix (B-36ba) make a single larger DONE manageable despite the whole-tree-materialHash vs active-main race. Batching multiplies the DONE-race cost for no correctness gain; omitting the selfcheck loses the anti-gaming freeze guard.

preMortem.scenario: A task survives in the repo but its inject() yields a payload the ground-truth does NOT catch
preMortem.trigger: a copy error or an inject()/payload mismatch during the apply
preMortem.consequence: a gamed corpus cell (payload would not be detected) biases the §6 results
preMortem.mitigation: corpus-selfcheck runs the inject() path and asserts ground-truth FAIL for every task; the build is blocked if any task does not show the exact PASS/PASS + PASS/FAIL pattern

preMortem.trigger: a miscount or a missing category during apply
preMortem.mitigation: corpus-selfcheck asserts total==24, 8 distinct categories, >=2 each, reading each task.json type

preMortem.scenario: The whole-tree-materialHash vs active-main DONE race stalls the merge
preMortem.trigger: main churns during the DONE pre-check
preMortem.mitigation: the now-merged B-6de6 storyFilesHash floor + B-36ba escalation gitCwd make freshness tolerant of unrelated drift; apply the pre-merge-main no-op + tight quorum window playbook if needed

preMortem.scenario: A stray/partial file is applied from /tmp/corpus-design
preMortem.trigger: an incomplete copy of a task dir
preMortem.mitigation: corpus-selfcheck asserts all 7 contract files present + the full invariant per task; npm test fails if any task is malformed
